stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many older European cities grew outward from a central marketplace, so their streets radiate like spokes and nearly every route leads toward the center. Many North American cities, ______, were laid out on a rectangular grid before settlers arrived, so their streets run in parallel lines and no single point draws traffic toward it.
explanation: Both sentences use the same frame: a group of cities, then how its streets are laid out. The subjects differ (European cities and North American cities), and the attribute flips: in one, streets radiate toward a center, and in the other, they form a grid with no center. Two things set side by side with opposite features call for a contrast word, so 'by contrast' is correct.

A.why: You saw a specific group of cities and assumed it illustrated the first sentence. But North American grid cities don't show streets radiating from a marketplace. They do the opposite, so they're a contrast, not an example.

C.why: 'Similarly' needs both groups to share the same feature. Here the street patterns are opposites, spokes versus a grid, so nothing similar is being described.

D.why: You read the second sentence as a result of the first. How European cities grew doesn't cause North American cities to use grids. The two are compared, and neither causes the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Dandelions produce lightweight seeds topped with tufts of fine bristles, so a single gust can carry them several kilometers from the parent plant. Oak trees, ______, produce heavy acorns that usually drop within a few meters of the trunk and travel farther only if a squirrel or jay carries them off.
explanation: Name the subject and attribute of each sentence. Dandelion seeds travel kilometers on the wind, while oak acorns drop within a few meters. The subjects differ and the attributes are opposites (far versus near), so the contrast word 'by contrast' is correct.

B.why: You picked an example word because a specific plant follows. But oaks don't illustrate wind-carried, far-traveling seeds. Their acorns do the reverse, so the oak is a contrasting case, not an instance.

C.why: 'Likewise' would mean acorns spread the same way dandelion seeds do. The passage says acorns stay near the trunk, which is the opposite attribute.

D.why: Nothing about dandelion seeds causes acorns to be heavy. You treated two side-by-side descriptions as cause and effect.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: During a heavy storm, a forested hillside absorbs much of the rainfall into its loose, root-filled soil and then releases that water to nearby streams gradually over several days. A paved parking lot, ______, absorbs almost none of the rain that strikes it, sending runoff into storm drains within minutes.
explanation: The two sentences set a forested hillside beside a paved parking lot. The hillside absorbs much of the rain and releases it slowly, while the lot absorbs almost none and sheds it within minutes. Different subjects with opposite attributes need a contrast word, so 'conversely' is correct.

A.why: A specific surface follows, so you reached for 'for example.' But a parking lot isn't an example of soil that absorbs rain slowly. It does the opposite, so it's a contrast.

B.why: 'In addition' adds another point that runs in the same direction. The parking lot doesn't add to the hillside's absorbing role. It reverses it.

D.why: 'Similarly' needs the same attribute in both sentences. Absorbing much and absorbing almost none are opposites, not matches.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In eighteenth-century England, wool was still spun largely in workers' cottages, where families fit the work around farm chores and set their own hours. Cotton, ______, was increasingly spun in water-powered mills, where a bell announced when the workday began and when it ended.
explanation: Each sentence names a fiber and says where and how it was spun. Wool was spun in homes on the families' own schedules, and cotton was spun in mills on a schedule set by a bell. The subjects differ and the working conditions are opposites, so 'by contrast' is correct.

A.why: Cotton is a specific case, so 'for instance' looked tempting. But cotton doesn't illustrate home spinning on flexible hours. It shows mill work on fixed hours, the opposite.

B.why: 'Thus' means the second sentence follows from the first. How wool was spun doesn't cause cotton to move into mills. The two are compared, and neither causes the other.

C.why: 'Likewise' would mean cotton was also spun at home on flexible hours. The passage says it was spun in mills on a bell's schedule, which is the reverse.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In many skilled trades, wages climb steadily with experience; a licensed electrician with fifteen years on the job typically earns about twice what an apprentice does. In many fast-food jobs, ______, pay stays nearly flat over time, and a worker with a decade of experience may earn only slightly more than someone hired last week.
explanation: The passage places two kinds of jobs side by side in the same frame: how pay changes with experience. In skilled trades it climbs steadily, and in fast food it stays flat. The subjects differ and the attributes are opposites, so 'conversely' is correct.

A.why: A specific kind of job follows a general claim about wages, so 'for example' felt natural. But fast-food pay doesn't climb with experience. It goes against the tendency, so it's a contrast, not an illustration.

C.why: 'Moreover' adds a point that supports the first. Flat pay doesn't strengthen the claim that pay climbs with experience. It points the opposite way.

D.why: Electricians' rising pay doesn't cause fast-food pay to stay flat. You treated a comparison as cause and effect.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Engineers who design river crossings choose among several bridge types, each suited to a different distance. Suspension bridges hang their roadways from steel cables draped over tall towers, which lets a single span stretch well over a kilometer. Beam bridges, ______, rest their roadways directly on a row of closely spaced piers and rarely span more than about eighty meters between supports.
explanation: Name each subject and its attribute. Suspension bridges hang from cables and span very long distances. Beam bridges sit on closely spaced piers and span only short distances. The two bridge types are described in the same frame, but the attribute flips from long to short. That is a difference between two parallel cases, so you need a contrast word: 'by contrast.'

A.why: You saw the opening line about 'several bridge types,' then saw one specific type, and called it an example. Beam bridges are not an illustration of what suspension bridges do. They work the opposite way, so this is a contrast, not an example.

C.why: 'Similarly' needs the same attribute on both sides. Here the support method and the span length are both opposite, so the two sentences do not match.

D.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that the passage never makes. Beam bridges' short spans are not a result of how suspension bridges are built. The two are simply set side by side.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In medieval Europe, linen was the everyday fabric of ordinary households. It was spun from flax, a plant that grew readily in cool northern fields, so most villages could produce their own cloth. Silk, ______, had to be carried thousands of miles along overland trade routes from Asia, and its cost kept it largely in the wardrobes of nobles and wealthy merchants.
explanation: Linen was made locally and worn by ordinary people. Silk was imported from far away and worn mainly by the wealthy. The two fabrics are described in parallel, but the attributes are opposites (local versus imported, common versus elite). 'Conversely' marks that difference.

A.why: You took silk to be a specific case of the everyday fabric just described. Silk does not illustrate linen's story. It reverses it, so this is a contrast, not an example.

B.why: 'Likewise' says silk shared linen's traits. In fact silk was imported and expensive where linen was local and cheap, which is the opposite.

D.why: Nothing about linen being grown locally causes silk to be imported. The sentences compare two fabrics, and neither one leads to the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most bony fish carry a swim bladder, a gas-filled sac they can inflate or deflate to hover at a chosen depth with almost no effort. Sharks, ______, have no swim bladder at all. To avoid sinking, they rely on large, oil-rich livers and on the lift produced as they keep moving forward through the water.
explanation: Bony fish have a swim bladder. Sharks have none. The subjects differ and the attribute flips from 'has' to 'lacks,' so the sentences set two cases against each other. 'By contrast' is the comparison-contrast word you need.

A.why: This is the trap. A specific animal follows a general statement, so it looks like an example. But sharks lack the very feature the first sentence describes, so they go against the claim instead of illustrating it.

B.why: 'In addition' adds a further point in the same direction. The second sentence does not add another fact about swim bladders. It describes an animal without one, which is a difference.

C.why: 'Thus' signals a conclusion drawn from the first sentence. Bony fish having swim bladders does not explain why sharks lack them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many perching birds learn their songs by listening to adult tutors during a brief window early in life, and young birds raised without a tutor produce garbled, incomplete songs. The eastern phoebe, ______, never needs a tutor. Ornithologists have found that phoebes raised entirely in isolation still sing their species' simple two-part song correctly.
explanation: The first sentence gives a general tendency: many perching birds must learn their songs from a tutor. The phoebe is one specific case, but it breaks the rule, because it sings correctly with no tutor. A case that goes against the tendency is a contrast, so 'by contrast' is right.

B.why: This is the trap. One specific bird follows a general claim, so you reached for 'for example.' But an example has to agree with the claim, and the phoebe does the opposite of what the first sentence describes.

C.why: 'Likewise' would mean the phoebe also depends on a tutor. The passage says it needs none, which is the opposite attribute.

D.why: Other birds' need for tutors cannot be the reason the phoebe needs none. The sentences compare two cases, and neither causes the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Printmakers sort their techniques by where the ink sits on the plate. In relief printing, such as woodcut, the artist carves away the areas meant to stay blank, and ink is rolled onto the raised surface that remains. In intaglio printing, ______, the image is cut into the plate, and ink is pressed down into those sunken lines while the top surface is wiped clean.
explanation: Both sentences describe a printing method in the same frame, and the attribute flips. In relief, ink sits on the raised surface. In intaglio, ink sits in the sunken lines and the surface is wiped clean. Two parallel methods with opposite ink placement call for 'conversely.'

A.why: You treated the second sentence as one more point in the same direction. It actually describes a method that inks the plate the opposite way, so this is a difference, not an addition.

B.why: 'Consequently' would make intaglio a result of how relief printing works. The two techniques are independent methods placed side by side.

D.why: The opening line names a category ('techniques'), so the next method can look like an instance of it. But intaglio is not an example of relief printing. It does the reverse, so you need a contrast word.
